_provenance.paper: A. V. Klimenko, S. E. Kuhn et al. (CLAS), 'Electron scattering from high-momentum neutrons in deuterium', Phys. Rev. C 73 (2006) 035212, arXiv:nucl-ex/0510032 (experiment 'Deeps', spokesperson S. Kuhn)
_provenance.source: CLAS Physics Database experiment eid = 90, quantity 'F2 * P(Ps)' ('Structure function times lab momentum distribution', dimensionless): the 115 measurement pages https://clas.sinp.msu.ru/cgi-bin/jlab/msm.cgi?eid=90&mid=<mid>&data=on, fetched 2026-09-23 (HTTP 200 each) and parsed from the 'Measured data' block (cos theta_pq, value, stat, syst).
_provenance.licence: no licence stated by the database (checked 2026-09-23); published measured values, transcribed with attribution
_provenance.convention: PER DEUTERON target, the reduced cross section of D(e,e'p_s)X: the measured cross section divided by the Mott cross section and a kinematic factor, = F2N(x*,Q2) x P(p_s, cos theta_pq), P the LIGHT-CONE spectator momentum distribution of the paper's Eq. (8) (paper Sec. V-VI). p_s and theta_pq are LAB (= deuteron rest frame) spectator momentum and angle to q. Q2 as labelled by the database; the blocks the database labels Q2 = 0.18-0.65 GeV^2 are kept verbatim and NOT interpreted (the paper, Sec. IV, bins Q2 in [1.2, 2.1] (average 1.8) and [2.1, 5.0] (average 2.8) GeV^2 only; what the smaller labels are is unverified).
_provenance.physics_caveat: p_s = 280-600 MeV/c is the HIGH-momentum tail, where the paper finds PWIA adequate only for cos theta_pq < -0.3 and FSI enhancement at transverse angles; it is NOT BONuS's p_s < 100 MeV/c window. This table is VENDORED for a proposed row and is NOT wired to any harness (phase_B1_spin_deuteron.md).
_provenance.normalisation_rules_sec8: rule 3: a reduced CROSS SECTION on the deuteron -- per nucleus in its normalisation, a structure function of the struck NUCLEON times a per-deuteron momentum distribution; any shape comparison must divide out F2N(x*) at fixed W*.
_provenance.ps_bins: the paper's five p_s bins have AVERAGES 0.30, 0.34, 0.39, 0.46 and 0.53 GeV/c (Sec. IV); the database labels the last one 560 MeV. Kept verbatim; a harness must use the paper's 0.53 or state which.
